note: A REQUEST to W1-01: no CSR address, opcode or bit position is assigned here (those come from the W1 CSR allocator). Logical names only.

carrier.access_note: write-only per Context is the design intent; the allowed access level is not frozen here
carrier.width_reason: the plan says 32 bits but no sourced bound or allocator output exists; not invented here

declaration.consumer: the first target-class instruction of the SAME Context, in program order, to reach E2

E1.name: request_park
E1.point: declared target is at the Context issue head, valid, and has NOT entered the shared RVV queue

E2.name: consume
E2.point: the beat the front end accepts the granted target instruction

ordering_rule: state_free recycles state but does NOT hand the instance over; only a reliably stored region_done wakes and grants a waiter

properties.U1: no early bind: writing the declaration CSR is not a tile side effect and does not trigger E1
properties.U2: no early consume: pending is not read by any consumer before E2
properties.U3: no late bind: once ARMED only the first target to reach E2 may consume it; after a redirect it is never re-attached to a later instruction
properties.U4: stall keeps pending: a parked head or a full front-end queue does not clear it, and a repeated csrw is an ARMED conflict
properties.U5: redirect/cancel clears pending, cancels the waiter and makes the head eligible again; a Context generation change clears it the same beat
properties.U6: wake is event driven after region_done, not polled each tick

faults.text: csrw while a declaration is already ARMED
REGION_START while ACTIVE, PARKED or ending
declaration kind is not in the closed set
tile touched with no ACTIVE region
tile touched after END was accepted
Task exits with an open region and no END
Task exits after END but before region_done
pending survived a Context generation change
target accepted with nothing ARMED
a parked target was accepted instead of staying at the head
START accepted before E1 granted a lease
second FIRST for a chain
CONTINUE for a chain that has no FIRST
FINAL for a chain that has no FIRST
accumulate or write on a chain after its FINAL
END while a chain has no FINAL
completion for an op that was never accepted
state_free before END
state_free with unsettled accepted ops
region_done before END
region_done with unsettled accepted ops
region_done before state_free
Context index outside the configuration
model raised a fault code the ABI does not define

fault_groups.F3: touch or free out of order after END
fault_groups.F4: task exit with an unfinished region

cleanup.grant_then_redirect: a grant already taken is SETTLED (instance released and waiters woken); 'not accepted' does not mean 'no side effect'
cleanup.waiter_then_redirect: the waiter is removed and the head becomes eligible again
cleanup.armed_then_redirect: pending is cleared; no later instruction inherits it
cleanup.accepted_then_cancel: accepted ops still settle for real; the region ends FAILED and never publishes a success region_done

mode_table_schema.carried_by: the sealed kernel manifest (W5), one table per kernel template; NOT a global whitelist

mtwiden_values.note: mtwiden is a 2-bit field (mtype[1:0]); 0 means unconfigured

disabled_mtwiden.decided_by: design W3 section 1 / W5 4.2.1: INT8 is registered as existing but disabled on the tensor path

limits.note: the front end CLAMPS tk and tm silently, so a table that asks for more is lying about what the hardware does

rules: inside an asm block any vset* is illegal
CLEARED -> mode must carry restore: true
tile use at CLEARED with no restore is MISSING_RESTORE_PREAMBLE
a disabled mode hit is DISABLED_MODE

corrections_to_design_text.text: The design lists vtype 18 / 265 / 256 for FP32 / BF16 / INT8. The upstream test constants are 0xD2 (210), 0x1C9 (457) and 0xC0 (192): they carry the ta/ma bits that msetmtype forces to 1 when mtwiden != 0. 18 and 265 are the same values with ta/ma cleared; 256 is NOT the INT8 vtype in any form.
The plan cites RvvFrontEnd.sv 131-135 for the accepted beat; the accepted expression is at line 116 and the registered valid_inst_q at 134.
The plan cites Decode.scala:1194 as the END decode (csrrwi). That line is the BitPat for csrrw, and no csrrwi pattern is named there; END is a W1/W2 helper whose encoding is not decided here.
msetmtype silently clamps tk by SEW (SEW16 -> 2, SEW32 -> 1, SEW8 -> 4) and tm to 16; a table row that asks for more describes hardware that does not exist.
mtype = tm[23:10] | tk[7:5] | mtwiden[1:0]. The 16384 in the compiler's formula is tm = 16 shifted by 10, not a flag bit.
every limit the mode-table checker relies on (the tk clamp per mtwiden, tm_max, mtwiden values, LMUL per SEW) carries its own sourced line; none is a bare constant in the validator.
